text: Well, that's a painful way to head into what's shaping up as a crucial divisional matchup: after Caleb Williams and the Bears outdueled Drake Maye in a 30-24 Thursday night loss, the Patriots are grappling with the uncomfortable reality that their turnover differential—one of Mike Vrabel's four foundational pillars—has become a genuine weakness, and they'll need to tighten that up considerably if they want to right the ship against Miami on Sunday at 4:15 PM ET. On the roster front, there's been some modest housekeeping: the team re-signed LB Jose Ramirez to the practice squad while releasing OL Jacob Rizy from the same squad and moving P Bryce Baringer from injured reserve. Meanwhile, Rhamondre Stevenson continues to do the thankless work that doesn't always show up on SportsCenter—he's knocking on the door of 100 carries for his sixth consecutive season and represents the kind of steady, underrated production that could prove essential in a close divisional battle. On a lighter note, Watertown High School's Coach Joey Carroll earned the Patriots Coach of the Week honors for steering the Raiders to a 31-14 victory, while the Navy-Notre Dame game arriving at Gillette Stadium brings a layer of college football tradition and Patriots historical connection to the stadium this season
